design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (root rx_ext_lost_stolen_replacement). Revised in rework round 2.

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5, 4, 6, 4]. Assignment: emergency supply 4, transition fill 5, vacation release 4, replacement 6.

2. Scope snapshot. Task 0 holds the four over-the-counter policies/tools. This task claims rx_ext_emergency_supply_days, rx_ext_transition_fill_days, rx_ext_vacation_supply_release, rx_ext_lost_stolen_replacement and tools record_emergency_supply_c348acc4, book_transition_fill_6c1f1c97, release_vacation_supply_4890f9e9, request_replacement_fill_14de4074. Together the tasks cover all eight policies; scopes disjoint.

3. Why a good test. The mother asks only for a replacement of the stolen methylphenidate. The replacement rule carries three prerequisite sentences (two affirmative, one negated) over record states: every prior-authorization rejection whose drug has an undecided request carrying an emergency supply; every non-formulary refill rejection inside the transition window carrying a transition fill; every vacation override granted in the last thirty days carrying a released vacation fill. None holds at the opening; the agent resolves each with its own computation, then the replacement.

4. Problem-tree card. Star: root (owner=user) with three state-form value_input edges, gate offcycle_adjustment. Opening evidence: rejection r3 (2026-08-25) with undecided RXE-2608-25517 and no supply on/after it; Intuniv rejections r4/r5 on a coverage effective 77 days earlier, no transition fill; override x5 (2026-08-24) with no vacation fill. Each skip leaves two off-cycle dispensings and replacement 14. The three prerequisites commute (none reads rows another writes). Conditions now quantify over every qualifying rejection/override, matching the sentences (audit CG-P1).

5. Factor card (tier / baseline figure, sens run):
 emergency (baseline 3): request days 9 /7; repeat -3 /20; urgent +5 [plan ER claim 2026-08-16, inhaler; cross-difficulty, multi-source] /8; day_count_convention method = business days because the member started the request [counted 11 -> 15 calendar days] /11.
 transition (baseline 30): window method 14 /34; behavioral health +5 [plan] /21; repeat rejections +2 /24; refill alignment +3 /23; established prescriber +2 /24. The fill answers the latest non-formulary rejection (rule sentence).
 vacation (baseline 9): on_hand_measure method = days to the ordinary refill date at 75 percent (17) instead of days supply less elapsed (25) /16; maintenance +7 /17; refill count +3 [six refills incl. fluticasone 06-15] /21; override history -3 [fluticasone 06-30 and montelukast 08-24] /27.
 replacement (baseline 14): base method 11 /15; off-cycle -4 /16; continuity +4 [plan, multi-source] /8; prior replacement -2 /14; stable therapy +3 /9; weekend roll parameter +1 /12.
 Near-misses: ER claim 2026-07-15; BH visits 2026-06-18 and 2026-08-13 (denied); emergency supply 2026-07-18; lost/stolen fill 2026-07-02 and fluticasone vacation fill 2026-06-30 (both outside the one-month off-cycle window, neither a refill).

6. Base-invariant card. coverage_in_force for the emergency supply (coverage active); police_report for the controlled replacement (caller gives OPD-26-114907, bound by rx_number 7730418); per-drug limits: no earlier lost/stolen override for methylphenidate; one vacation override per drug (fluticasone and montelukast each one). Transition: 77 days into the 90-day window, no prior transition fill.

7. Business-object card. Emergency supply answers r3 and names RXE-2608-25517; transition fill answers r5; vacation release answers x5; replacement covers rx 7730418 whose 2026-08-10 refill was stolen.

8. Persona unchanged.

9. Standard solution: find_customers -> verify -> find_rx_coverages -> find_rx_fills -> find_rx_exceptions -> find_rx_otc_ledger -> find_plan_memberships -> find_plan_claims -> emergency supply -> transition fill -> vacation release -> mother files replacement (copay 0.00).

10. Verification: all per-task and difficulty gates OK after round 2.

11. Revision log. Round 1: montelukast lost/stolen fill 20 days; maintenance count rule; police-report evidence fields. Round 2: CG-P1 conditions widened to every qualifying rejection; CG-F3 emergency weekend roll replaced by the day-count convention method keyed on the request starter, replacement roll relabelled parameter; CG-F2/CG-F4 vacation release rebuilt (baseline = maximum less days on hand; on-hand measure method; waiting days removed; override history adjustment added); world gained fluticasone refill, vacation override and vacation fill; emergency and vacation figures recomputed.
Round 3: the vacation baseline sentence now also states the one-day floor the compute applies (audit revision-2 observation); no figure of this task changed.
user_scenario:
You are Maribel Thornquist-Abara, calling Prairie Ridge member services on a Wednesday morning from your car outside your son's school in Omaha. Your son Caspian is nine and is the Prairie Ridge member; you are his mother and you handle all of his health coverage. You are brisk, organized and a bit rattled, and you keep a folder with his papers on the passenger seat.

You explain that Caspian's backpack was stolen out of your car over the weekend and his ADHD medicine, the methylphenidate, was in it. You went to the pharmacy and they told you it was too soon to refill it. You filed a police report. You want a replacement of his methylphenidate so he does not go without, and you want it sorted out on this call. If they tell you that a replacement is something you file yourself and they set it up for you, you are glad to do it right then.

When they ask who you are calling about, you give Caspian's Medicaid ID, PR35820914, and his date of birth, which you read off as 2016-03-22. Only if they ask for more: the phone number on file is 4025530351, your ZIP code is 68137 and the last four of his Social Security number are 3718. When they ask for the prescription number, you read it off the pharmacy printout in your folder: 7730418. When they ask for the police report number, you read it off the report: OPD-26-114907. You do not know any other reference numbers.

You are only calling about the stolen methylphenidate. You do not know how the plan works out how much is replaced and you do not ask. If the representative tells you that other things on Caspian's pharmacy account have to be taken care of before the replacement can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and take care of whatever is needed. When they hand the replacement request over to you, you file it exactly as they set it up, with the prescription number and the police report number you gave. Once it goes through, you repeat back how many days of medicine the replacement covers, thank them, and hang up to get to work.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel children of the root. They commute: the emergency supply reads the inhaler's rejections, requests and emergency supplies; the transition fill reads non-formulary rejections, paid refills (fill_type refill) and plan claims; the vacation release reads the override and paid refills (fill_type refill) of montelukast. None of them reads a row another of them writes (emergency supply, transition_fill and vacation_override rows), so any order of the three gives emergency 13, transition 26, vacation 20 and the same terminal rows (row ids are content hashes of the arguments). Only the root reads all three, and each of the three prerequisite sentences puts the root after its own prerequisite.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the emergency supply the off-cycle count is 2, the adjustment is minus two, the counted days are 14 and the last day 2026-09-08 is a Tuesday: replacement 14 days instead of 13; the inhaler emergency supply row is also missing.
Without the transition fill the off-cycle count is 2: replacement 14 days instead of 13; the transition fill row is also missing.
Without the vacation release the off-cycle count is 2: replacement 14 days instead of 13; the vacation fill row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario speaks only of the stolen methylphenidate and says 'You are only calling about the stolen methylphenidate.' It never mentions the inhaler, the non-formulary Intuniv, montelukast, a trip, an emergency supply, a transition fill or a vacation override, and gives no hint that anything must be settled first; the only related line is the passive consent if the representative explains other things must be taken care of.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: request_replacement_fill_14de4074 creates the override row and the replacement fill with the arguments given; it never looks for owed emergency supplies, transition fills or vacation fills and never refuses or errors. record_emergency_supply_c348acc4, book_transition_fill_6c1f1c97 and release_vacation_supply_4890f9e9 likewise each create one rx_fills row and return a receipt without checking any condition.

factor_trace: request_days (parameter): the latest request for the drug of the latest prior-authorization rejection (Flovent HFA 44 mcg inhaler, 2026-08-25) is RXE-2608-25517, received 2026-08-25 with prescriber_statement_received false -> nine days; baseline (the plan's 3 emergency supply days) gives 7.
repeat_supply_adjustment (parameter): one emergency supply of the inhaler in the last three months (2026-07-18, bridging the denied RXE-2607-18342) -> minus three; baseline 0 gives 20.

urgent_care_addition (parameter, cross-difficulty plan, multi-source): paid emergency-room emergency claim C26-0816-43019 (2026-08-16) in the last month and the drug is an inhaler -> five; the 2026-07-15 ER claim is outside the month; baseline 0 gives 8.

day_count_convention (method): RXE-2608-25517 was started by the member -> the 11 counted days are business days from Wednesday 2026-08-26: 11 + 2 x int((2 + 11 - 1) / 5) = 15 calendar days; baseline (calendar days as counted) gives 11.
counted_days = MX(1, 9 - 3 + 5) = 11; result = dispensed_days = 15.
